subject: Pre-bill question: geo proration & sampling window for unexpected Q1 overage
messages:
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia@datahelix.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected jump in embed tokens — pre-bill check

Hi Marcus,

We're reviewing the pre-bill for Q1 and noticed a ~45% jump in embed token usage the week of 2028-03-21 compared to our baseline. We've attached a sampling export (sampling-export-202803.zip) and the provisional invoice PDF. Can you confirm whether Redwood changed the sampling window or geo-attribution logic for multi-entity tenants recently?

Quick context: we're multi-entity (EU / US), and the net VAT treatment for March depends on whether those tokens are attributed to the EU entity. If the ingestion classification shifted, that will alter our VAT liability and the invoice total.

We're trying to avoid a payment hold, so any immediate clarifications are appreciated.

Thanks,
Sofia Ramos
Billing Operations — DataHelix
sofia@datahelix.com

Attachments: sampling-export-202803.zip (csv), invoice-draft-Q1-2028.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia@datahelix.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected jump in embed tokens — pre-bill check

Hi Sofia — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the export. Looping in Vanessa from Billing and Ben from Sales Ops to triage.

Initial checks: we did an infra change rolled 2028-03-20 that tightened geo-sampling for region tagging (low-risk change intended to reduce orphaned sessions). It shouldn't increase counted tokens — it typically reduces duplicates. That said, there are a couple of edge cases where routing to a different entity tag causes tokens to be re-classified into another billed entity and affects VAT.

Vanessa / Ben — can you pull the per-entity attribution for DataHelix for 2028-03-15 -> 2028-03-28 (hourly) and validate the sampling-window parameter set used last month vs what the export shows? Also, if attribution changed from US->EU for a large bucket, we should decide on proration vs retro credit.

Sofia — we'll target a diagnostic within 48 hours and propose an interim credit if our logs show a clear attribution shift. If not, we'll share the sampling logs so your finance team can reconcile.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Manager — Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Sofia Ramos <sofia@datahelix.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected jump in embed tokens — pre-bill check

Hi all — I pulled the attribution and sampling-window logs. Findings summary: 

- Change note: on 2028-03-20 we flipped the region-tag-fallback rule from "closest-geo" to "tenant-preference" for certain dedicated tenants; DataHelix was included in that roll.
- Effect: for ~18 hours (03/21 02:00–20:00 UTC) ~6.2M embed tokens previously attributed to the multi-entity US bucket were re-tagged to the EU entity. This explains the spike on your export.
- Cause: an unexpected tenant-preference override for a subset of streaming ingest sessions (we have the request IDs).

Recommendation: because this was a classification change (not additional generation), we propose a proration path: retro-attribute the 6.2M tokens back to the original US entity for billing, and issue a corrective invoice reflecting EU VAT only on legitimately EU-attributed traffic. This preserves contractual VAT boundaries and minimizes disruption to your cash flow.

If you prefer not to retro-attribute, alternate paths: (a) issue a one-time VAT wash adjustment (credit equal to estimated VAT delta), or (b) let the charge stand and open a formal compliance review.

I've attached a short export of the request IDs and hourly attribution slices (attached as contract-schedule-A.pdf here for reference).

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Billing Operations — Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com
Attachments: contract-schedule-A.pdf (attribution-slice-summary)
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Sofia Ramos <sofia@datahelix.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Apr 2028 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected jump in embed tokens — pre-bill check

Adding procurement context from our side. Per the contract (Schedule A, section 2.3) the billing entity mapping is authoritative but allows for mutual corrections for operational misattribution discovered within 90 days. Given that this window is open, we can proceed with Vanessa's retro-attribute + corrective invoice flow.

Action items I propose: 
- Vanessa to provide a redline-ready corrective invoice by EOB Thu 2028-04-05. (Vanessa: can you include the VAT delta calculation and line-by-line attribution?)
- Marcus to confirm acceptance with DataHelix and get an acknowledgement email to avoid collection hold.
- Finance/Legal: finalize language for the credit so it reconciles with your EU VAT reporting.

I'll also attach a DocuSign acknowledgement template for quick sign-off (https://www.docusign.com/link/abc123-invoice-ack).

Ben Carter
Sr. Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
Attachments: invoice-ack-docusign-template.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia@datahelix.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Apr 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected jump in embed tokens — pre-bill check

Hi Sofia — quick note to confirm next steps and timeline so your team can decide on the payment flow: 

- Vanessa will send a corrective invoice and an attachment with the hourly attribution export by EOB today (we've prioritized the redline).
- If you agree, sign the DocuSign acknowledgement to confirm Redwood will apply the retro-attribute correction and issue a credit for the VAT delta. The DocuSign link is in Ben's note. Signing will unblock collection holds on your account.
- If you need more time, please let us know by EOD Mon 2028-04-09 and we'll keep the provisional invoice on hold while we finish the audit.

Let me know if your finance team needs a short call — we can schedule one tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Manager — Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
